item.title: ‘Connections wide and deep’: Melania Trump puts Hunter Biden on $1B notice over Jeffrey Epstein link; calls claims ‘false and defamatory’
item.description: Melania Trump has issued a $1 billion legal notice to Hunter Biden, alleging defamation related to claims he made about her connection to Jeffrey Epstein. Trump demands Biden retract his statements, issue an apology, and remove the content. Her attorney asserts Biden's claims are false, disparaging, and widely circulated, threatening legal action if he doesn't comply.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: UFC cage fight 2026: Is Ivanka set to host the White House event - Here’s what Donald Trump wants
item.description: Donald Trump is reportedly planning a UFC cage fight on the White House lawn for America's 250th Independence anniversary in 2026. Despite stepping back from politics, Trump wants his daughter, Ivanka, to be involved in the planning and organization of the event. Ivanka's potential participation would mark her return to public events after a three-year break.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Michigan mishap: Pickup truck surpasses stop sign, collides with a van; 6 dead
item.description: A devastating collision in Gilford Township, Michigan, resulted in at least six fatalities after a pickup truck disregarded a stop sign and crashed into a van carrying ten passengers. Multiple individuals were ejected from both vehicles, and seven survivors were transported to a hospital for treatment.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: California redistricting battle: ‘Historic’ maps to end Trump presidency, claims Gavin Newsom; calls president as Donald ‘Taco’ Trump
item.description: California Governor Gavin Newsom announced the state will redraw congressional maps, aiming to help Democrats regain control of the House and potentially impact the next presidential election. This move comes as a response to Texas Republicans' redistricting efforts, which could bolster their majority in the House. Draft maps are expected soon, with Newsom planning a press conference with prominent Democrats.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 2-1 judgment: Appeals court allows Trump admin to cut billions in foreign aid; overturns lower court ruling
item.description: A divided US federal appeals court has allowed the Trump administration to proceed with billions of dollars in cuts to foreign assistance programs, overturning a lower court ruling. The decision reverses a previous order that would have required the restoration of aid funds approved by Congress for fiscal year 2024.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: For the first time in history, an entire country might move its whole population; the reason will shock you
item.description: Tuvalu, a Pacific island nation of 11,000, faces potential relocation due to rising sea levels. NASA reports a 15 cm rise in sea levels around Tuvalu in the last 30 years, threatening habitability by mid-century. Challenges include infrastructure risk, freshwater scarcity, and economic disruption. Tuvalu is also planning to become the first digital nation, preserving its culture and sovereignty virtually.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: This virus is turning rabbits into ‘zombie bunnies’ with horn-like growths — can it spread to dogs or cats?
item.description: A strange virus is affecting wild rabbits in America. It causes horn-like growths on their faces. These rabbits are called 'zombie bunnies'. The virus is Shope papillomavirus or SPV. It spreads through contact and insects. The virus impacts rabbit health. It makes them vulnerable to predators. The virus does not infect humans or other pets.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Trump vs Harvard: University nears $500M settlement to restore federal fundings; resolve months-long feud
item.description: Harvard University and the Trump administration are reportedly nearing a $500 million settlement to restore federal funding and end investigations that began with antisemitism concerns. The deal, still under negotiation, follows funding cuts and lawsuits, with some Democrats warning against setting a precedent of yielding to political pressure. Other universities like Columbia and Brown have also reached similar settlements.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Trump warns Putin of 'very severe consequences' if Russian-Ukraine war continues: calls talks with EU a '10/10'; Zelenskyy claims Putin is 'bluffing'
item.description: President Trump warned Putin of severe consequences if the Ukraine war doesn't halt after their Alaska summit. This followed a virtual meeting where Zelenskyy downplayed Putin's military strength and the impact of sanctions, urging a ceasefire. European leaders, backing Zelenskyy, emphasised the need to protect their security interests, while Trump hinted at potential land swaps, a proposal Ukraine firmly rejects.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Kennedy Center Honors recipients 2025: From George Strait to Michael Crawford - who will be awarded by Trump
item.description: President Trump has announced his first Kennedy Center Honors recipients, including George Strait and Sylvester Stallone, while also unveiling plans to renovate the venue. Trump, who now oversees the center, intends to restore its prestige and grandeur for America's 250th anniversary. His increased involvement has sparked controversy, leading to programming changes and criticism from the arts community.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Air Canada staff strike: Protest set to begin this weekend - why attendants rejected a 38% pay hike
item.description: Air Canada faces potential major travel disruptions as flight attendants overwhelmingly voted to strike, leading the airline to issue a lockout notice. The union demands fair wages, cost-of-living adjustments, and boarding pay, while Air Canada claims to have offered a substantial pay increase.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Immigration crackdown: Venezuelan civic groups sue Trump admin over termination of Temporary Protected Status; call it cruelty towards vulnerable
item.description: Venezuelan civic groups and migrants are challenging the Trump administration in Boston federal court over the termination of Temporary Protected Status (TPS). The lawsuit, filed against US immigration agencies, alleges the abrupt cancellation of TPS protections, expanded under former President Biden, disrupts lives and risks deportation.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Former Platters band member Sandra Hall goes missing, last seen on Friday in Brooklyn; search under way
item.description: Sandra Hall, 80, a former member of The Platters, has been missing since Friday after boarding a subway in Brooklyn. Suffering from dementia, her family is deeply concerned and following up on a possible sighting in the Bronx. Hall, who joined The Platters in 1965, was last seen wearing gray pants, white sneakers, and a pink shirt.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed sends firefighting team to aid Albania’s wildfire battle
item.description: In August 2025, Albania faced severe wildfires. The United Arab Emirates sent a specialized firefighting team. They provided personnel, helicopters, and equipment. The team assisted in areas like Petrela and Gramsh. UAE's President directed urgent climate assistance. Other nations like Czechia and Greece also helped. International cooperation was critical. Efforts focused on protecting communities and the environment.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Road safety improves sharply in Kuwait: Accidents down 45%, deaths down 34% in first half of 2025
item.description: Kuwait experienced a significant improvement in road safety during the first half of 2025. Traffic accidents plummeted by 45%, and fatalities decreased by 34% following the implementation of a stringent new traffic law in late April. Traffic offenses also declined by 16%, indicating a positive shift towards safer driving behaviour.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Kuwait: No more minimum salary requirement for family visit visas, what expats need to know
item.description: Kuwait has eliminated the minimum salary requirement for family visit visas, allowing all expatriates to invite extended relatives up to the fourth degree without income restrictions. Applications are processed quickly through the new Kuwait Visa platform. Visitors can arrive by any airline or transport mode. This change complements recent reforms, including instant tourist visas on arrival for GCC residents, boosting regional travel and family reunions.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Turkish Airlines and Oman Air frequent flyer partnership: Travelers can now earn miles across both airlines
item.description: Oman Air and Turkish Airlines have launched a strategic Frequent Flyer partnership starting August 1, 2025. Members of Turkish Airlines’ Miles&Smiles and Oman Air’s Sindbad programs can now earn and redeem miles across both airlines’ extensive networks. This collaboration expands travel benefits, offering seamless mileage accrual on flights between Oman, Türkiye, Europe, and beyond, enhancing loyalty rewards for frequent travelers.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Take our capital back’: Nearly 800 troops deployed by Donald Trump arrive at DC; 23 individuals arrested overnight
item.description: President Trump deployed National Guard members to Washington, D.C., asserting federal control over the city's police to combat what he claims is rampant lawlessness, despite data indicating otherwise. This action follows Trump's vow to relocate homeless individuals and criticisms of local spending. Mayor Bowser pledged cooperation while highlighting the city's limited autonomy under federal law, marking a contentious intervention.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Bahrain stands tall: Ranks 3rd in Arab region in new UN Human Development report
item.description: Bahrain secures third rank among Arab nations in the 2025 UN Human Development Report. Globally, Bahrain holds 38th position with an HDI score of 0.899. The report highlights Bahrain's progress in health, education, and income. UAE and Saudi Arabia rank higher in the region. The HDI measures life expectancy, education levels, and income.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: UAE: What is Abu Dhabi's ‘Hayat’ program? How it enabled 1,090 life-saving organ transplants since 2017
item.description: Abu Dhabi has completed 1,090 organ transplants since launching the ‘Hayat’ programme in 2017, with a record 290 in 2024 alone. Major hospitals have led medical breakthroughs, including the UAE’s first combined heart-lung transplant. The Hayat programme encourages residents aged 21 and above to register as organ donors, aiming to save lives and advance ethical transplantation practices.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk
